trickyParts: The fork read's mark (epoch, foreign) is taken inside srv.Apply before EncodeStateAsUpdateV1, and copied into a local in applyLive right after forkLive, so a later joined read cannot pair an operation's rendering with another read's counters.

ygo encodes the whole delete set in every update, so a write's rendering is reused only on the room instance its fork was read from: cold forks record no mark, and recover/keepReplica draw a process-unique epoch.
loadedHead is load.head, not the cursor start: versions roomLoad.took recorded during the load are durable but not in the loaded document.
The ranking's Appendix A ignore lists drop applyLive samples at this base (applyLive runs under MarkQuote.func1 and applyOpsUnconditional.func1), so shares are cumulative focus without them.
deviations: The first implementation, its tests and the environment were lost with the pod's disk before any push; the production code was rebuilt by the implementer from the verified, simplified diffs of that first implementation (not delegated to a worker), and the tests were rewritten by a worker and re-verified, including all four negative controls.
Path counters live on Service (renderPathCounts) rather than split over renderedReplica and liveWrite.
The warm outside-schema repair takes path (A) (r.markdown nil counts as changed, as rendering would), not 'render' as the plan's table says; classification and WARN are as before.
Memory compared on a forced-GC heap profile from one extra base/head pair rather than the end-of-step profile of the median runs, which held in-flight request allocations.
W6/W12 shares measured without the ranking's ignore lists (see trickyParts).
discoveredComplexity: INFRA-642 also adds a field to liveWriteOrigin and a branch in renderedReplica.observe; its implementer was told the field names (rendering, inRoom); whichever merges second adapts.
